newsitem.title: MEXICO: MIT's Dornbusch says Mexico peso too strong - paper.
newsitem.headline: MIT's Dornbusch says Mexico peso too strong - paper.

text.p: U.S. economic guru Rudiger Dornbusch criticised the monetary policy of Mexico's central bank Wednesday in an interview with the daily newspaper Reforma.
"The Banco de Mexico is bad news for the the peso, not the people who predict that there will be difficulties, difficulties which then happpen," Dornbusch said.
Dornbusch, who correctly predicted the 1994 peso devaluation, has recently said the peso is once again too strong in real terms against the dollar. The peso has weakened sharply in recent sessions.
"It is the moment to talk about it (the peso's strength) just as it was in 1993, before things get serious," he said.
Dornbusch refused to talk about specific people in the central bank who were managing the country's monetary policy, but did said the institution had a "long history" of bad management of the peso.

"It is probably the most distinguished history in this sense of any country in Latin America," Dornbusch said in the interview. The Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) professor is in Mexico for a three-day conference on international finance.
